summary: Explore the Pastoria Master Suite renovation of Koos de Keijzer and Clemence Harvey’s off-grid home, featuring Italian travertine, Studio Bagno’s Milady pan and serene country views.
title: Pastoria Master Suite Renovation. A Serene Country Scene.
bodyHtml:
Pastoria Master Suite renovation. A serene country scene.

The off the grid home of Koos de Keijzer and Clemence Harvey was originally designed by local architect and built in 2000 out of granite from the property. Many rocks in the external stonewall veneer have lichen and moss on them.

The house has solid architectural bones. North facing and running east to west, the master bedroom and ensuite, are on the western side of the house and have a tendency to heat up with the western setting sun. A linear zig zag is the original floor plan of the house. This ‘lightning bolt’ configuration had many strange nooks, odd internal spaces. Their aim with the subsequent renovations was to capture these vacant spaces and put them to good use.

This was achieved in the master bedroom by creating a separate entrance and turning a previous awkward office space into the master bathroom. From an interior planning perspective, space was obtained wherever possible.

Punching upwards and outwards, adding the height in ceiling, adding top windows and skylights to allow for extra light flow and ventilation, and extending out the master bedroom windows deeper wider while an adding a window seat.

One of the most captivating aspects of the property is the view, and the view from the Master suite is the best that the house offers. Koos and Clemence were keen not to compete with the serenity of the view and yet imbue the glamor of a hotel ensuite.

A dramatic 4-meter-high open entrance opens from the bedroom into the Italian travertine clad enclave of the Master suite.

Sandstone coloured travertine was selected after visiting Roma’s Six Senses thermal baths designed by Patricia Urquila. Articolo ‘Scandal’ sconces were specified either side of the bathroom mirror. Studio Bagno was selected for contemporary porcelain ware. The ‘Milady’ lavatory features no cistern that sits unobtrusively from the wall. The bathing tub (much needed after hours of gardening) is placed in a sea of travertine.

Rugs specified from loom finish off the tactile feeling underfoot and the 8-meter-long wardrobe appointed by Moltini & C.

“We wanted to achieve a sense of privacy and understated luxury separate to the rest of the house. We were keen to open and brighten up the space while embracing the spectacular view. Being avid travellers, we have had the opportunity to experience many bedroom and bathroom plans. So, the ease between these two spaces is what we wanted to achieve and we think we have.”

Architect Koos de Keijzer
